Bhagavad Gītā|2.50: One joined to understanding leaves behind, here and now, both good and bad deeds. So give yourself to yoga: yoga is skill in action.
Bhagavad Gītā|3.30: Give all your actions up to me, with your mind on the self. Free of wanting, free of 'mine', fight, with your fever gone.
Bhagavad Gītā|2.67: When the mind follows the roaming senses, it carries off a person's judgement, as the wind carries a boat on the water.
Bhagavad Gītā|3.21: Whatever the best person does, others do too. Whatever standard he sets, the world follows.
Bhagavad Gītā|18.6: Even these acts should be done without attachment and without wanting their fruit. This, Pārtha, is my settled and highest view.
Bhagavad Gītā|1.21: Then, O king, Arjuna said these words to Kṛṣṇa: 'Acyuta, stop my chariot between the two armies.'
Bhagavad Gītā|3.11: Nourish the gods with this, and let the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will reach the highest good.
Bhagavad Gītā|4.9: Whoever truly knows my divine birth and work is not born again when he leaves the body, Arjuna. He comes to me.
Bhagavad Gītā|1.46: If the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, weapons in hand, killed me in battle, unarmed and not fighting back, that would be better for me.
Bhagavad Gītā|2.37: Killed, you will win heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kuntī, resolved to fight.
Bhagavad Gītā|2.41: Here the resolute mind is single, joy of the Kurus. The thoughts of the irresolute branch without end.
Bhagavad Gītā|14.11: When the light of knowledge shines from every gate of this body, know that goodness (sattva) has grown.
Bhagavad Gītā|14.25: The same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, giving up every undertaking: he is said to have gone beyond the three qualities.
Bhagavad Gītā|2.14: The touch of the senses, son of Kuntī, brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These come and go and do not last. Bear them, Bhārata.
Bhagavad Gītā|4.23: For one who is free of attachment, released, his mind set in knowledge, acting as an offering, all his action melts away.
Bhagavad Gītā|7.3: Among thousands of people, hardly one strives for perfection. Of those who strive and succeed, hardly one knows me as I am.
Bhagavad Gītā|9.34: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow to me. Joined to me like this, with me as your goal, you will come to me.
Bhagavad Gītā|3.18: He has nothing to gain here by acting or by not acting, and he depends on no being for anything.
Bhagavad Gītā|9.2: This is the king of knowledge, the king of secrets, the highest purifier: seen directly, right, easy to practise, and lasting.
Bhagavad Gītā|13.8: Detachment from the objects of the senses, freedom from ego, and seeing the evil in birth, death, old age, sickness and pain.
Bhagavad Gītā|5.10: One who acts, placing his actions in Brahman and giving up attachment, is not stained by sin, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
Bhagavad Gītā|11.1: Arjuna: 'Out of kindness to me you spoke the highest secret, about the self. Your words have cleared my confusion.'
Bhagavad Gītā|11.28: As the many currents of rivers rush toward the sea, so these heroes of the world of men pour into your blazing mouths.
Bhagavad Gītā|13.27: Whoever sees the highest lord present equally in all beings, undying among the dying, truly sees.
Bhagavad Gītā|11.55: Whoever works for me, holds me highest, is devoted to me, free of attachment and without hatred for any being, comes to me, son of Pāṇḍu.
Bhagavad Gītā|17.20: A gift given because giving is right, to someone who cannot repay it, at the right place and time, to a worthy person: that gift is called pure (sāttvika).
Bhagavad Gītā|18.65: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
Bhagavad Gītā|14.18: Those in goodness rise upward; those in passion stay in the middle; those in darkness, held by the lowest quality, go down.
Bhagavad Gītā|2.45: The Vedas deal with the three qualities. Rise above the three, Arjuna: beyond opposites, always steady in goodness, not caring to gain or keep, master of yourself.
Bhagavad Gītā|12.12: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. Peace follows giving up.
Bhagavad Gītā|17.7: Even the food each person likes is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and giving. Hear how they differ.
Bhagavad Gītā|13.10: Steady devotion to me with no other aim, a liking for lonely places, and no taste for crowds.
Bhagavad Gītā|12.4: Holding all the senses in check, even-minded everywhere, glad in the good of all beings, they too reach me.
Bhagavad Gītā|11.12: If the light of a thousand suns rose in the sky at once, it might match the light of that great being.
Nirvāṇa-bhakti|5: Lord Nemi, Pradyumna, Śambukumāra and Aniruddha, with seventy-two crore and seven hundred others, reached liberation on Mount Ūrjayanta (Girnar).
Nirvāṇa-bhakti|2: Twenty of the Jinas, praised by gods and demons, free of all affliction, reached nirvāṇa on the peak of Sammeda hill. Homage to them.
Nirvāṇa-bhakti|18: The five hundred sons of King Yaśodhara in Kaliṅga, and a crore of sages on the Koṭiśilā rock, reached nirvāṇa. Homage to them.
Kundakunda, Samayasāra|18: In the same way, one who seeks liberation should know the soul as a king, trust it, and then follow it.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|1: Lord of speech, known by the thousand and eight auspicious marks, we praise you with a thousand and eight names, to reach what we long for.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|117: Names of the Jina: of endless power, who cannot be cut, destroyer of the three cities, the three-eyed one, whose sight is perfect knowledge.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|87: Names of the Jina: firmly set, whole, at rest in himself, free of dust and disturbance, unstained, spotless, free of passion and of longing.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|124: You are the self of the five highest principles and lord of the five auspicious events. You know the six kinds of substance, and you hold together the seven points of view.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|39: Names of the Jina: beyond counting, pure of mind, full of virtue, doer of good, whose teaching is good; a garden of dharma, a home of virtues, who ends both merit and sin.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|19: Names of the Jina: golden-navelled, the self of all beings, who bears and sustains them; the source, the mighty, the shining; being itself, and the end of rebirth.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|100: Names of the Jina: shining like molten gold, lofty, bright as the rising sun and as fire, golden as an evening cloud, glowing like heated gold.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|112: Names of the Jina: the great teacher, lord of words, conqueror of desire, who knows all things; fair of body, yet free of the body; the well-gone, who destroys false views.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|123: You alone are the light of the worlds. You see and know (the two kinds of awareness). You are the one path to freedom in three parts, with the four infinite gifts risen from within.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|127: A devotee who recites this hymn with care is made pure. Whoever reads it through becomes a vessel of blessing.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|92: Names of the Jina: beloved of the three worlds and worthy of their worship, the dawn of their blessing, whose feet their lords adore, the crest-jewel at the top of the three worlds.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|105: Names of the Jina: treasure of the highest good, the ground of all, resting on nothing yet firmly set; steady, unmoving, firm as a pillar; vast, renowned and broad.
Jinasena, Jinasahasranāma|107: Names of the Jina: a mass of splendour, of endless strength, an ocean of knowledge and of virtue; full of radiance, of boundless light, light in bodily form, remover of darkness.
Caitya-bhakti|3: May the Jain teaching triumph, flowing in waves of viewpoints, showing that every substance arises, passes and lasts. Opening the barred door to matchless joy, may it grant liberation, pure, without loss, without end.
Caitya-bhakti|4: To the Arhats, the Siddhas, the teachers, the preceptors and the monks, worshipped by the whole world: homage, everywhere, to them all.
Caitya-bhakti|8: In thought, word and body I honour the shrines of the Jinas, praised by the three worlds, in the halls of the gods, in the heavens, among the stars and spirits, and in the world of men.
Caitya-bhakti|21: I honour the images of the Jinas, bathed in the light of jewels from the gods' crowns, which they serve step by step to reach perfection.
Samādhi-bhakti|11: Everywhere we fix our minds on 'arham', the sacred syllable that names the supreme beings, the true seed of the circle of the perfected.
Śānti-bhakti|11: The divine tree, the shower of heavenly flowers, the drum, the throne, the far-heard voice, the parasol, the pair of fly-whisks and the halo: these shine around him.
Śānti-bhakti|1: The summer sun, spreading its fierce, burning rays over the earth, makes people long for moonlight, water and shade.
Amitagati, Sāmāyikapāṭha|23: Friend, neither a bed of grass, nor the world's worship, nor the company of the order brings calm of mind. So always delight in the self, and let go of every outward craving.
